defects: Drops the general linear order α and PseudoEMetricSpace E of the gold, specializing to f : ℝ → ℝ with the standard metric, which changes the class of the theorem (not the same generality).

Does not formalize 'total variation' at all: the gold LHS is eVariationOn f (u '' Iic n), the supremum-based variation over the sequence's image set, whereas the produced LHS is just ∑ |f(x_{i+1}) - f(x_i)|, a plain finite sum. This discards the core mathematical content (that the sup-defined variation collapses to this sum for a monotone sequence) and turns the statement into a near-tautology equating |a-b| with dist(a,b) on ℝ.

Never references an image set (gold's u '' Iic n) or the ambient order/metric structure the variation is computed over — the notion of 'variation along a monotone sequence of points in a metric space' is absent.

The hypothesis h_mono (∀ i : Fin n, x i ≤ x (i.castSucc)) is malformed/trivial: x has type Fin (n+1) → ℝ but i has type Fin n, so 'x i' requires an implicit coercion; if that coercion is castSucc (as used explicitly on the RHS of the inequality), the hypothesis reduces to x (i.castSucc) ≤ x (i.castSucc), a vacuous tautology rather than expressing monotonicity between consecutive points x_i ≤ x_{i+1}.

As written, LHS and RHS of the produced conclusion are equal merely by the definition of dist on ℝ (dist a b = |a - b|), so the theorem is essentially trivial/definitional rather than the substantive equality asserted by the gold.
